evals.prompt: Why is the handler in evals/files/order-handler.ts so hard to follow? Our reviewer says its cognitive complexity is way too high. Break it down for me.
evals.expected_output: An explanation built from the scorer's breakdown: handler scores 32, with each increment tied to its line and the deep nesting (customer branch, product loop, nested ternary) named as the main contributors.
expectations: Ran scripts/score.mjs on the file rather than estimating
States the handler's score as 32
Accounts for the increments line by line, including the nesting penalties (e.g. the if at line 24 costs +4 at nesting 3)
Names the deepest nesting (if/else inside the for...of inside the customer branch) and the nested ternary as the biggest contributors
Suggests at least two concrete refactors (e.g. guard clauses, extracting the line-pricing loop, a coupon lookup map)

evals.prompt: Refactor syncInventory in evals/files/inventory.ts so it passes our complexity limit of 15. Keep the behaviour exactly the same.
evals.expected_output: syncInventory rewritten with async/await, guard clauses and small extracted helpers; every function in the file scores 15 or less (ideally 10 or less), with before → after scores reported.
expectations: Reports the before score of syncInventory as 26, computed with the scorer
Re-ran the scorer after the refactor and reports after scores for syncInventory and every extracted function
Every function in the refactored file scores 15 or less according to scripts/score.mjs
The exported signature syncInventory(skus, dryRun) and its resolved value shape are unchanged
Preserves the dry-run behaviour, the null-qty logging, and the single retry on Throttled, or on Timeout when retryable

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript AWS Lambda handler for POST /refunds: parse the JSON body {orderId, amountCents, reason}, validate it, load the order from DynamoDB via a getOrder(orderId) helper, reject refunds over the order total or on orders older than 30 days, call issueRefund(), and map errors to 400/404/409/500 responses.
evals.expected_output: A handler split into small functions (parse/validate, policy checks, error mapping), each scoring 10 or less, with the scorer run before finishing.
expectations: Ran scripts/score.mjs on the written file before finishing
Every function in the produced code scores 10 or less according to scripts/score.mjs
The handler orchestrates and delegates parsing, validation and error mapping to separate named functions
Uses guard clauses or early returns instead of nested if/else for validation failures
